owner_approval: 2026-10-18, in chat: 'yes set up the avoid list and test the reddit one'
why_this_exists: The owner asked whether social media could catch booms. Published evidence says retail attention spikes precede UNDERperformance: Barber, Huang, Odean & Schwarz (JF 2022) find Robinhood herding predicts about -4.7% over 20 days; Bradley et al. (RFS 2024) find WallStreetBets research predicted returns only before the GameStop squeeze. This project's A25 found the same sign for firms newly naming hot leaders. This tests, on our own universe and data, whether a WallStreetBets attention surge marks a stock to AVOID. A buy signal is not tested: every source points the other way.

data.source: Arctic Shift public Reddit archive API (arctic-shift.photon-reddit.com), endpoint /api/posts/search/aggregate, aggregate=created_utc, frequency=week, subreddit=wallstreetbets, title=<ticker>; JSON only, no files executed
data.chunking: one request per ticker per calendar year; a year that times out is split into quarters; a ticker with any chunk still failing is excluded and counted

universe: issuers ever in the top 1,000 by 63-day median dollar volume (close >= $5) on any day 2017-2025, one symbol per CIK from the price catalogue, alphabetic, at least 3 letters, and not a lowercase entry in /usr/share/dict/words (so CAT, LOW, NOW, ALL are excluded as ambiguous)

event.hype_week: a week with at least 10 WallStreetBets posts with the ticker in the title AND at least 5 x the ticker's mean weekly count over the prior 26 weeks (prior mean floored at 1)
event.deduplication: at most one event per ticker per 13 weeks (the first)
event.entry: the close of the first trading day at least one day after the week's end

outcome: the stock's return over h trading days minus the mean of 50 random liquid same-SIC2 firms with no event in the same week (A24's control)
declared_sign: NEGATIVE (attention-induced overpricing reverses). Long-only use: an avoid rule. A positive result is reported as a refutation, not inverted into a buy rule.
significance: event-level, block bootstrap over event months (block 3), 4000 draws, two-sided
pass_rule_per_trial: design mean < 0 with p < 0.025 AND holdout mean < 0 AND the design mean stays negative after dropping the 10 most negative events AND |design mean| > 50 bps
positive_control_reported_first: mean absolute return of event stocks in the hype week vs the same stocks' typical week: attention surges should coincide with big moves; if they do not, the ticker matching is broken
known_weaknesses_declared_up_front: Title keyword match: a ticker can appear in a title for unrelated reasons; 3+ letters and the dictionary filter reduce, not remove, this.
Posts only, not comments: the daily discussion threads carry much of the volume; titles capture what was salient enough to post about.
Liquid stocks only ($5, top 1,000): the most extreme meme names are often below these bars at the start of their run.
Survivorship in the price panel as A19.
amendment_2026_10_18_before_any_reddit_d: Per-ticker server-side aggregation timed out at every window above one quarter and was throttled (HTTP 422 'Timeout. Maybe slow down a bit'), so no count was ever received for the test. Replaced by a polite crawl of every r/wallstreetbets post 2017-01-01 to 2025-12-31 via /api/posts/search (fields created_utc,title; 100 per request; >= 1.5 s apart; backing off on 422/429), stored as monthly gzip JSON lines under data/wsb_attention_v1/posts/. A post counts for a ticker if its title contains the ticker as a whole word in UPPER case, optionally prefixed by '$' (e.g. 'NVDA', '$NVDA'); 'Nvidia' does not count. Weekly buckets are Monday-Sunday UTC. Everything else -- universe, event rule, controls, trials, windows, pass rule -- is unchanged.
